text: Name a pharaoh of ancient Egypt.
flavor: They built their tombs to last forever and sealed them with curses. Some of the curses were meant.
rules: Any king or queen who ruled Egypt as pharaoh, from the first dynasties to Cleopatra. A name that several pharaohs shared counts for the best known of them.

answers.lore: A minor king made immortal when Howard Carter found his tomb almost untouched in 1922.
Ruled for 66 years. Shelley's poem 'Ozymandias' is about him.
The last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt, and the first of her Greek dynasty to learn Egyptian.
Built the Great Pyramid, the tallest human-made structure on Earth for nearly 4,000 years.
Swept away the old gods for a single sun disc, the Aten. His successors tried to erase him from history.
One of the few women to rule as pharaoh, often shown wearing the royal false beard.
Akhenaten's queen. Many scholars think she ruled after him, under another name.
His Step Pyramid, designed by Imhotep, is the oldest large stone building in Egypt.
His carved palette may show the moment Upper and Lower Egypt became one kingdom.
Son of Cleopatra and, she said, Julius Caesar. Killed in 30 BC at seventeen: the last pharaoh.
The first woman known for certain to have ruled Egypt as pharaoh.
Said to have reigned for over 90 years, the longest reign in history, though scholars now doubt it.
His pyramid holds the oldest known Pyramid Texts: spells to lift a dead king to the stars.
Probably the 'Shishak' of the Bible, who plundered Jerusalem.
Herodotus says he sent Phoenician sailors all the way around Africa.
The last native Egyptian pharaoh, who fled the Persians in 343 BC.
The Rosetta Stone is a decree in his honour.
Crowned pharaoh in 332 BC. The oracle at Siwa hailed him as son of Amun.
Called 'the Brave', he began the war that his son Ahmose finished, driving the Hyksos out of Egypt.
A shadowy ruler from before the first dynasty, known from a carved mace head. Hollywood made him the Scorpion King.
Possibly the first woman to rule Egypt, around 2950 BC.
A foreign Hyksos king who shared his name with Apophis, the serpent of chaos.
Herodotus says she drowned her brother's killers in a flooded banquet hall. She may never have existed.

traps.reason: Raised in Pharaoh's court, but never pharaoh himself.
The genius behind Djoser's pyramid, later worshipped as a god. Never pharaoh.
Ramesses II's beloved queen, with a stunning tomb. A queen, never pharaoh.
Amenhotep III's powerful queen, never pharaoh.
A monument, not a king. It probably wears Khafre's face.
Cleopatra's lover and, she said, Caesarion's father. Never pharaoh.
An astronomer of Roman Egypt, not a king.
A film monster. The real mummies were real kings.
Tutankhamun's wife and half-sister, a queen but never pharaoh.
Hatshepsut's steward and architect, never pharaoh.
Cleopatra's daughter. She became queen of Mauretania, not Egypt.

source: Copied from the daily question "pharaohs" on 28 November 2026.
